- The cards I have are decent but not explosive for a multiplayer game
- Angel of Finality is good but at {3}{W} requires both W and G sources

- Turn 1: Can play Mishra's Factory untapped (good) or a tapped land

- To cast Abundant Growth ({G}) on T2, I'd need to have played Factory and then put Fertile Ground or Abundant Growth on it
- To cast Fertile Ground ({1}{G}), same issue
 
I'm leaning toward keeping the hand because it has potential mana fixing and a decent early creature strategy. I'll need to be strategic about mana usage and color allocation, focusing on ensuring I can cast my key spells efficiently. The Angel's graveyard removal ability could be particularly valuable against opponent strategies that rely on graveyard interactions.

While the initial mana development seems limited, the presence of color-fixing options and a solid creature base provides some flexibility. The tapped lands suggest a slightly slower start, but the overall potential for mid-game disruption and creature presence makes the hand playable.

I'll weigh the trade-offs carefully, considering the need for mana stability against the strategic value of the cards in hand.

annotations.description: As part of Brainstorm resolution, GLM47 is putting a card back on top of their library. They chose Terramorphic Expanse, but they have Azorius Chancery in hand which is a tapped land that bounces a land - less immediately useful. More importantly, they should consider putting back their worst cards. With only 2 lands in play (both tapped), they need to develop mana. Terramorphic Expanse is actually a reasonable land to put back since it can be drawn and played to fix mana/thin the deck. However, putting back Argentum Armor (a 6-mana equipment with 6 equip cost - extremely expensive and uncastable for many turns) would be better, as it's a dead card for the foreseeable future. They still need to put back a second card after this one, so context matters, but Terramorphic Expanse is a playable land they may want soon whereas Argentum Armor is nearly unplayable in the early game.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Terramorphic Expanse on top of library with Brainstorm
annotations.betterLine: Put Argentum Armor on top of library (completely dead card costing 6 to cast and 6 to equip), keeping Terramorphic Expanse as a playable land drop for mana development

annotations.description: Put Puresteel Paladin back on top of library with Brainstorm instead of more expensive, less castable cards. Puresteel Paladin (WW) could be cast soon with Azorius Chancery + mana fixing from Abundant Growth/Fertile Ground, and it synergizes with the equipment plan. Argentum Armor (6 mana to cast, 6 to equip) is far more dead weight.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Puresteel Paladin back on top of library as one of the two Brainstorm tuck cards
annotations.betterLine: Put back Argentum Armor and Angel of Finality (the two most expensive, least castable cards), keeping Puresteel Paladin in hand for the equipment synergy plan

annotations.description: Azorius Chancery's ETB trigger requires returning a land to hand. GLM47 chose to return Halimar Depths, which is a tapped land that only produces {U}. However, Mishra's Factory is a more valuable utility land (can become a 2/2 creature), and Azorius Chancery itself already produces {W}{U}. Returning Halimar Depths means replaying it next turn (it enters tapped again), losing a turn of mana development. But the real consideration is that returning Mishra's Factory would let you replay it untapped next turn for immediate {C} production, while Halimar Depths enters tapped and only gives {U} which Azorius Chancery already covers. On the other hand, Halimar Depths gives a scry-like effect when it re-enters, which has some value. Given the hand contains Sol Ring, Ebony Fly, Fertile Ground, and Abundant Growth, the player wants to cast Sol Ring (costs {1}) and potentially Abundant Growth or Fertile Ground soon. Returning Mishra's Factory and replaying it untapped next turn would give access to more mana sooner. However, returning Halimar Depths to get the top-3 rearrange effect again when replayed is defensible. This is close to reasonable but slightly suboptimal since Mishra's Factory untapped would have been better for mana development.
annotations.actionTaken: Returned Halimar Depths to hand from Azorius Chancery's ETB trigger
annotations.betterLine: Return Mishra's Factory to hand, as it can be replayed untapped next turn for immediate mana access, while Halimar Depths enters tapped and the Chancery already covers the blue mana needs

annotations.description: GLM47 is discarding to hand size (8 cards, max 7). Argentum Armor costs 6 to cast and 6 to equip (12 total mana), making it extremely expensive and slow. However, Sol Ring is in hand and hasn't been played yet - with only 2 lands on board, Sol Ring would be a critical accelerant. The discard choice of Argentum Armor is actually reasonable given how expensive it is, but there's a question of whether Angel of Finality (a 4-mana creature with a situational ETB) might have been a better discard since the deck appears to be a Galea equipment/aura deck where Argentum Armor could eventually be cast from the top of library. That said, without Galea on the battlefield yet, and given the massive mana investment Argentum Armor requires, this is a defensible choice. The real question is why Sol Ring wasn't played this turn - but that's a separate decision not being evaluated here.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Argentum Armor to hand size
annotations.betterLine: Discarding Angel of Finality might be slightly better since it's a mediocre 4-mana 3/4 with a situational graveyard exile ETB, while Argentum Armor has higher ceiling if the game goes long or if Galea is found to cast it from library top. However, this is close and Argentum Armor's massive cost makes it a reasonable discard too.

annotations.description: Chose Transmogrifying Wand over Thran Dynamo when the board has no threatening creatures requiring immediate removal. annotations.actionTaken: Cast Transmogrifying Wand (3 mana, sorcery-speed creature removal with 3 charges)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Thran Dynamo (4 mana, taps for 3 colorless) to ramp into Oblivion Sower next turn, which is a much higher-impact play

annotations.description: GLM47 played Halimar Depths (a tapped land) instead of casting Sol Ring with the available mana. With Azorius Chancery tapped and Mishra's Factory untapped, they had access to 1 colorless mana from Mishra's Factory, which is exactly enough to cast Sol Ring. Sol Ring is one of the most powerful mana accelerants in the game and should almost always be deployed as early as possible. Playing it now would allow significantly more mana next turn. Halimar Depths enters tapped and provides no immediate mana benefit - it could have been played next turn instead after deploying Sol Ring this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Halimar Depths as their land for the turn instead of casting Sol Ring first.
annotations.betterLine: Tap Mishra's Factory for {C}, cast Sol Ring, then play Halimar Depths as the land drop. This way they get both Sol Ring and Halimar Depths this turn, having significantly more mana available next turn.

annotations.betterLine: Take only Command Tower, which produces useful colorless mana. Skip Azorius Chancery since it produces unusable {W}{U} mana and forces bouncing a land.

Additionally, they already have a Wastes in hand, so bouncing Wastes would give them a land to replay while keeping the superior mana source on the battlefield.
annotations.actionTaken: Returned Command Tower to hand from Azorius Chancery's ETB trigger
annotations.betterLine: Return Wastes to hand instead, keeping the more versatile Command Tower on the battlefield

annotations.description: Casting Duskmantle Seer before activating Aminatou's +1 is a sequencing error. Activating Aminatou first draws a card (putting one back), potentially finding a better play or more information before committing 4 mana to a creature that has a symmetrical downside and is vulnerable to Transmogrifying Wand and Oblivion Stone.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Duskmantle Seer before using Aminatou's loyalty ability
annotations.betterLine: Activate Aminatou's +1 first to draw a card and see options, then decide whether to cast Duskmantle Seer or hold up resources based on what was drawn.

annotations.description: With 5 mana available (Island, Silverbluff Bridge, Mountain, Mind Stone, Oblivion Stone - though Oblivion Stone is likely being held for its activation), the player chose Commander's Sphere (3 mana) over Padeem, Consul of Innovation (3U = 4 mana). Padeem gives all artifacts hexproof, protecting the valuable Oblivion Stone and Mind Stone from removal, and provides card draw at upkeep if you control the highest CMC artifact. With Oblivion Stone (CMC 3) already on board and Commander's Sphere about to enter, Padeem's upkeep trigger could be relevant. However, Padeem at 4 mana would use Island + Silverbluff Bridge + Mountain + Mind Stone, leaving nothing untapped. Commander's Sphere at 3 mana leaves mana open and ramps, which is also reasonable given the expensive cards in hand (Herald of Anguish at 7, Brudiclad at 6, Scavenged Brawler at 6). The ramp from Commander's Sphere helps cast these expensive threats sooner. Still, Padeem protecting Oblivion Stone (a key board wipe) while providing card advantage seems like the stronger play in a 4-player game where artifact removal is common.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Commander's Sphere for ramp
annotations.betterLine: Cast Padeem, Consul of Innovation to protect artifacts (especially Oblivion Stone) with hexproof and potentially draw cards on upkeep

annotations.description: Aminatou, the Fateshifter is a value engine that will generate card advantage every turn. Attacking into the player for 8 damage (39→31) while leaving Aminatou alive allows her to continue accumulating value. The Oblivion Sower's 5 power alone would likely kill Aminatou if she's at 3-4 loyalty.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked Gem3F Optim directly with both Matter Reshaper and Oblivion Sower for 8 damage
annotations.betterLine: Send at least the Oblivion Sower at Aminatou to kill her (5 damage vs likely 3-4 loyalty), and optionally send Matter Reshaper at the player for 3 damage. Removing Aminatou prevents ongoing card advantage and flickering.

annotations.description: Playing Mortuary Mire (which enters tapped) over Isolated Watchtower is debatable. Mortuary Mire's ETB lets you put a creature from your graveyard on top of your library, but Gem3F Optim has no creatures in their graveyard, so the ETB trigger is wasted. Isolated Watchtower would at least provide colorless mana and has a useful activated ability, especially since opponents like KimiK2 likely control more lands. However, Mortuary Mire does produce black mana which could be relevant, and the player may be planning to play Isolated Watchtower next turn. The Duskmantle Seer in hand costs 2UB and Gem3F already has color access through signets and Command Tower, so the black mana from Mortuary Mire isn't strictly necessary.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Mortuary Mire with no creatures in graveyard, wasting its ETB trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Play Isolated Watchtower instead, saving Mortuary Mire for later when there might be a creature in the graveyard to recur. Isolated Watchtower provides immediate untapped mana and a useful scry/ramp ability.

Mishra's Factory hasn't been activated to become a 2/2 Assembly-Worker yet, so this ability has no valid target and accomplishes nothing. The player is wasting Mishra's Factory's tap for no benefit.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Mishra's Factory's '{T}: Target Assembly-Worker creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn' with no Assembly-Worker on the battlefield.
annotations.betterLine: Either activate Mishra's Factory to become a 2/2 Assembly-Worker first (option 2) and then potentially use the +1/+1 ability from another source, or simply tap it for {C} mana (option 1) to use toward casting a spell this turn, or leave it untapped for future use.

annotations.description: GPT5m Romance chose to activate Mind Stone (presumably to sacrifice it and draw a card) during their precombat main phase instead of playing the Swamp from hand first. They have a Swamp in hand and should play their land drop before spending mana on other actions. Additionally, with 6 mana available (Island, Silverbluff Bridge, Mountain, Mind Stone, Oblivion Stone could be tapped but Commander's Sphere too), they could potentially cast Padeem, Consul of Innovation (3U) this turn if they play the Swamp first and use their mana efficiently. Sacrificing Mind Stone for a card draw when you have powerful 4-drops to cast seems like it wastes a mana source prematurely. Playing Swamp first and then casting Padeem (using Island + Silverbluff Bridge for U, Mind Stone for C, Commander's Sphere for U = 3U) would develop a meaningful threat that gives artifacts hexproof and draws cards.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Mind Stone (likely sacrificing to draw) before playing their land for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp first, then cast Padeem, Consul of Innovation using the available mana (Island, Silverbluff Bridge, Mind Stone, Commander's Sphere can produce 3U). This develops a strong board presence that protects artifacts with hexproof and can draw extra cards.

annotations.description: Attacking Aminatou (at loyalty 3-4) with both Matter Reshaper (3/2) and Oblivion Sower (5/8) is likely overkill for removing the planeswalker. Combined they deal 8 damage to a planeswalker that likely has 3-4 loyalty. The Oblivion Sower alone (5 power) could remove Aminatou, while Matter Reshaper could chip away at Gem3F's life total or another opponent. Alternatively, attacking Gem3F directly with both creatures would pressure the weakest life total (31 hp) and deal 8 damage. While removing Aminatou has value (preventing flicker shenanigans and ultimate), using 8 power to kill a 3-4 loyalty planeswalker wastes significant damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked Aminatou, the Fateshifter with both Matter Reshaper and Oblivion Sower (8 total power against a ~3-4 loyalty planeswalker).
annotations.betterLine: Attack Aminatou with just Oblivion Sower (5 power is enough to kill it) and send Matter Reshaper at Gem3F Optim's face for 3 damage, or attack Gem3F with both creatures for 8 damage to pressure the lowest life total.

annotations.description: Duskmantle Seer is a 4/4 flyer that could attack any opponent for 4 unblockable damage with no risk. No opponent has an untapped flying or reach creature that could block it. Passing up free damage in a multiplayer game slows down the clock unnecessarily.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose not to attack with Duskmantle Seer.
annotations.betterLine: Attack the most threatening opponent (likely KimiK2 at 38 life with the strongest board, or any opponent) with Duskmantle Seer for 4 free flying damage.

annotations.description: With 5 lands and 8 cards in hand (likely exceeding the 7-card maximum hand size at end of turn), casting Sol Ring is fine but the sequencing could be better. Sol Ring costs 1 mana, but more importantly, the player should consider what they want to deploy this turn. With Sol Ring providing 2 colorless mana, they could potentially cast more spells. However, the real issue is that they have Abundant Growth and Fertile Ground which are land enchantments that cantrip or ramp - casting Abundant Growth first (costs G) draws a card and fixes mana, and Fertile Ground (costs 1G) ramps. Given they'll need to discard to hand size, they should prioritize deploying as many permanents as possible. Sol Ring is a strong play, but casting Abundant Growth on a land first (to draw a card and potentially find a land or see more options) before committing to Sol Ring would have been slightly better sequencing since they're going to overflow on hand size regardless.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Sol Ring
annotations.betterLine: Cast Abundant Growth first (on Exotic Orchard or Forest) to draw a card and potentially enable more plays, then cast Sol Ring with remaining mana, then potentially cast Fertile Ground or Ebony Fly to deploy more permanents before discarding to hand size.

annotations.description: GLM47 activated Mishra's Factory to become a 2/2 creature during their postcombat main phase while Sol Ring is on the stack (being cast). This wastes 1 mana to animate a land that can't attack (combat is over) and serves no purpose. The mana spent on animating Mishra's Factory could have been used more productively, and there's no reason to make it a creature at this point - it just exposes it to creature removal.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Mishra's Factory's {1} ability to become a 2/2 Assembly-Worker artifact creature during postcombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Tap Mishra's Factory for {C} mana instead to help cast Sol Ring or save the mana for casting other spells from hand like Ebony Fly, Fertile Ground, or Abundant Growth.

annotations.description: GPT5m sacrificed Commander's Sphere to draw a card during combat on turn 7, when they have only 3 lands and an Oblivion Stone on the battlefield. They have Seat of the Synod and Reliquary Tower in hand (two land drops available), plus expensive cards like Herald of Anguish (7 mana), Brudiclad (6 mana), Scavenged Brawler (6 mana), Padeem (4 mana), and Muzzio (3 mana). Commander's Sphere was their only mana rock remaining and provided crucial mana acceleration and color fixing. With only 3 lands + Oblivion Stone, sacrificing the Sphere sets them back significantly on mana development. They need to ramp toward casting their expensive threats, not sacrifice mana sources for card draw when they already have a full hand of 9 cards with no way to cast most of them.
annotations.actionTaken: Sacrificed Commander's Sphere to draw a card during combat, losing a mana source while already having 9 cards in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Tap Commander's Sphere for mana instead (or simply keep it as a mana rock). With a hand full of expensive spells and only 3 lands on board, the mana acceleration is far more valuable than drawing a 10th card. They should focus on deploying lands and ramping toward casting Padeem or Muzzio.

annotations.description: GPT5m is discarding down to hand size and chose to discard Muzzio, Visionary Architect, Hedron Archive, and Reliquary Tower. Muzzio is a powerful card advantage engine that synergizes extremely well with their artifact-heavy strategy and commander (Mishra, Eminent One). With Oblivion Stone, Prophetic Prism, and future artifacts, Muzzio could dig deep into the library for free artifacts. Hedron Archive is solid ramp and card draw. Meanwhile, Scavenged Brawler is a 6-mana creature that's less impactful in this deck, and cards like Oni-Cult Anvil are low-impact at this stage. Discarding Muzzio over Scavenged Brawler or Oni-Cult Anvil is a significant mistake - Muzzio provides repeatable card advantage that scales with artifact mana values, while Scavenged Brawler is just a beater (though its graveyard ability has value). The Reliquary Tower discard is also questionable when they have no maximum hand size issues and could have kept Seat of the Synod (an artifact land that enables Mishra and metalcraft) while discarding the basic Island instead - but Seat of the Synod was kept. Overall, discarding Muzzio is the main error.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Muzzio, Visionary Architect, Hedron Archive, and Reliquary Tower
annotations.betterLine: Should have discarded Scavenged Brawler (expensive, less synergistic), Oni-Cult Anvil (low impact without sacrifice fodder), and Reliquary Tower, keeping Muzzio and Hedron Archive which provide much better card advantage and ramp for the artifact strategy

Meanwhile, tapping it means it can't be used for mana on the next turn cycle (opponent turns), and it's being risked unnecessarily in combat where it could be blocked and killed for no benefit.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Ornithopter of Paradise, a 0/2 creature that deals no damage.
annotations.betterLine: Don't attack with Ornithopter of Paradise. Keep it back as a mana source and potential flying blocker. Only attack with Oblivion Sower (5/8) which actually deals meaningful damage.

annotations.betterLine: Discard Scavenged Brawler, which has a useful graveyard exile ability (putting +1/+1 counters and keyword counters on a creature), or discard Mountain since they already have red sources and desperately need the black mana from Crumbling Necropolis to cast their key spells.

With 15 power of flyers and opponents at 34-36 life, attacking could set up lethal in 2-3 turns rather than giving opponents more time to develop.

annotations.betterLine: Attack with all three flyers (or at minimum Enigma Sphinx and one other) at the most threatening opponent. Even with Sower of Discord's symmetry concern, 15 flying damage is too much to leave on the table.

Alternatively, if keeping Strionic Resonator, at least play the land first to not waste the land drop opportunity with proper sequencing.

annotations.description: Bounced Seat of the Synod (artifact land) instead of a tapped Mountain. Seat of the Synod is an artifact that synergizes with Herald of Anguish's Improvise, Padeem's artifact count/hexproof, and Mishra (commander). A tapped Mountain produces only red mana which Izzet Boilerworks already covers, and bouncing it loses no mana this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Bounced Seat of the Synod to hand from Izzet Boilerworks trigger
annotations.betterLine: Bounce a tapped Mountain instead, preserving the artifact land for Improvise synergy with Herald of Anguish and other artifact-matters cards in hand

annotations.description: KimiK2 Hothead had enough attack damage (claimed 19) to eliminate GPT5m Romance who was at 15 life, but instead attacked Gem3F Optim at 25 life, leaving them alive at 6. Eliminating a player in multiplayer is significantly more valuable than dealing non-lethal damage, as it removes an entire player's future turns and threats.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked Gem3F Optim (25hp), dealing non-lethal damage and leaving all three opponents alive.
annotations.betterLine: Attack GPT5m Romance (15hp) to eliminate them from the game entirely, reducing the number of opponents and their future threat potential.

annotations.description: KimiK2 Hothead activated Tomb of the Spirit Dragon's second ability to gain 1 life per colorless creature, but controls zero creatures. This spent {2} and tapped the land to gain exactly 0 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Tomb of the Spirit Dragon's life-gain ability with no colorless creatures on the battlefield, gaining 0 life for 3 mana.
annotations.betterLine: Simply tap Tomb of the Spirit Dragon for {C} if mana was needed, or leave it untapped. The 2 mana spent on this activation was wasted for zero benefit.

annotations.description: Gem3F Optim blocked Bane of Bala Ged (7/5) with only one 4/4 Angel token, leaving the Bane alive at 1 toughness. Bane of Bala Ged exiles a permanent each time it attacks, making it a must-kill threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked with a single 4/4 Angel token, which deals only 4 damage to the 5-toughness Bane, leaving it alive.
annotations.betterLine: Block with two Angel tokens to deal 8 damage total, killing the Bane of Bala Ged. Only one Angel would die (7 damage split as 4+3), trading one 4/4 token to permanently remove a devastating attacker.

annotations.description: Choosing to consume the Creature card type rather than Artifact. With powerful creatures potentially available and artifacts being lower-impact mana rocks, consuming the creature type sacrifices more potential value.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to consume the Creature card type
annotations.betterLine: Consume the Artifact card type instead, preserving the ability to use/cast creature cards which tend to be higher impact in this board state

annotations.description: Crystal Ball only provides scry 2 per turn, while Primordial Mist would generate a 2/2 creature token each end step plus the ability to play manifested cards. With only 1 card in hand and no board presence, Primordial Mist provides significantly more value.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Crystal Ball over Primordial Mist
annotations.betterLine: Cast Primordial Mist to generate recurring board presence and card advantage

annotations.description: KimiK2 Hothead activated Tomb of the Spirit Dragon's life-gain ability ({2}, {T}) with zero colorless creatures on the battlefield, gaining 0 life while spending 2 mana and tapping the land for nothing.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Tomb of the Spirit Dragon's second ability to gain 1 life per colorless creature, but controlled no colorless creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Tap Tomb of the Spirit Dragon for {C} instead, preserving the 2 mana that was wasted on a 0-life-gain activation.

annotations.description: Casting Rancor on Mishra's Factory in the postcombat main phase accomplishes nothing - the Factory reverts to a non-creature land at end of turn, causing Rancor to fall off and return to hand. This wastes mana for zero benefit.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Rancor targeting Mishra's Factory, which will stop being a creature at end of turn
annotations.betterLine: Hold Rancor in hand and cast it on a future turn when there's a permanent creature to enchant, or at minimum before combat on a future turn when Factory can attack with the bonus.

annotations.description: Enchanting Mishra's Factory with Fertile Ground is suboptimal. Mishra's Factory is a utility land that can become a creature, and when it animates and is destroyed in combat, the Fertile Ground aura would be lost. Additionally, all of GLM47's lands are tapped, so they can't benefit from the enchanted land this turn regardless. A better target would be Exotic Orchard or one of the basic lands - lands that are less likely to be destroyed and provide more reliable mana fixing. Exotic Orchard in particular already produces any color an opponent's land could produce, and enchanting it with Fertile Ground would give an additional mana of any color. Azorius Chancery would also be excellent since it already produces two mana, and adding Fertile Ground would make it produce three mana total when tapped.
annotations.actionTaken: Enchanted Mishra's Factory with Fertile Ground
annotations.betterLine: Enchant Azorius Chancery or Exotic Orchard with Fertile Ground for more reliable and efficient mana production without risking the aura if the land animates and dies

annotations.description: Declined Primordial Mist's end step trigger to manifest the top card of library for free. This is a pure upside ability that creates a 2/2 creature at no cost, with potential to be flipped face-up later. In a game where Gem3F needs board presence against two opponents at 15 life each, every free resource matters.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined all options including the free manifest from Primordial Mist
annotations.betterLine: At minimum, activate Primordial Mist's end step trigger to manifest the top card of library for free. Could also consider exiling the face-down Enigma Sphinx to potentially cast it.

annotations.description: Declined Primordial Mist's end step trigger, which provides a free manifest (2/2 creature) at no cost. This is pure upside with no downside. Additionally, the face-down Enigma Sphinx could potentially have been flipped or exiled for value.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without activating any abilities at end of turn.
annotations.betterLine: At minimum, activate Primordial Mist to manifest the top card of the library for free, gaining a 2/2 body with potential to be flipped face-up later.

annotations.description: KimiK2 activated Tomb of the Spirit Dragon's life gain ability while controlling zero colorless creatures, spending {2} and tapping the land to gain 0 life. This wastes 2 mana that could have been used toward casting Hangarback Walker or other plays.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Tomb of the Spirit Dragon's {2}, {T} ability to gain 0 life (no colorless creatures on board).
annotations.betterLine: Simply tap Tomb of the Spirit Dragon for {C} if mana was needed, or save the mana for casting Hangarback Walker from hand.

annotations.description: Gem3F Optim cast Ninja of the Deep Hours from hand for {3}{U} during precombat main, but has a face-down manifest creature (Enigma Sphinx) on the battlefield. With no opposing creatures on the board, the manifest would almost certainly go unblocked, allowing Ninjutsu for {1}{U} - saving 2 mana, getting the combat damage draw trigger, and returning the manifest to hand (which could then be cast as Enigma Sphinx later).
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Ninja of the Deep Hours from hand for full cost {3}{U} in precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Attack with the face-down manifest creature, then if unblocked, activate Ninjutsu {1}{U} to put Ninja of the Deep Hours onto the battlefield attacking, draw a card from the combat damage trigger, and return the manifest (Enigma Sphinx) to hand for future casting

annotations.description: Both opponents have all lands tapped, meaning there's minimal threat this turn cycle. Crystal Ball (cost {3}) could have been deployed now to start improving card quality, while Utter End could be held up next turn when all lands are untapped.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without casting anything, presumably to hold up Utter End mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Crystal Ball for {3} while opponents are tapped out, then hold up Utter End next turn with full mana available.

annotations.description: Gem3F Optim has 7 Angel tokens (4/4 flyers) and a Manifest creature on the battlefield. GLM47 Grudge is at 15 life with all lands tapped and no creatures. KimiK2 Hothead is at 15 life with all lands tapped and no creatures. GPT5m Romance is already eliminated at -1 life. Attacking with all 7 Angel tokens (28 flying damage) would be lethal against either remaining opponent, and splitting attacks could kill both opponents simultaneously (e.g., 4 Angels at one player for 16 damage and 3 Angels at the other for 12, or any combination that deals 15+ to each). Both opponents have no blockers and are tapped out. This was a missed lethal opportunity to win the game.
annotations.actionTaken: Gem3F Optim skipped the attack phase entirely, sending no creatures to attack.
annotations.betterLine: Attack GLM47 Grudge with 4 Angel tokens (16 damage, lethal against 15 life) and KimiK2 Hothead with 4 Angel tokens (16 damage, lethal against 15 life) to win the game on the spot. Even attacking all at one player guarantees killing at least one opponent.

annotations.description: KimiK2 has no creatures on the battlefield, making Tyrite Sanctum's activated abilities completely useless. Arch of Orazca would provide the same colorless mana plus a card draw ability once city's blessing is achieved (they control 8 permanents, need 10). The reasoning incorrectly references a Metalwork Colossus that isn't in play.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Tyrite Sanctum based on giving indestructible to a nonexistent creature
annotations.betterLine: Play Arch of Orazca for the card draw potential, which helps rebuild from an empty board at 15 life

annotations.description: With Utter End on the stack (likely targeting the manifest or Primordial Mist), Gem3F declined to use Primordial Mist's ability to exile the face-down Enigma Sphinx face-up, which would have allowed casting it this turn. With 0 cards in hand and 8 untapped lands producing the right colors (4WUB = 7 mana), casting Enigma Sphinx with cascade would have been a massive value play, especially given their empty hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate Primordial Mist's ability to exile the manifested Enigma Sphinx face-up
annotations.betterLine: Activate Primordial Mist to exile the manifested Enigma Sphinx face-up in response to Utter End, then cast Enigma Sphinx for 4WUB to get a 4/4 flyer plus cascade value

annotations.description: In a 1v1 situation, Gem3F declined to block what appears to be Mishra's Factory (a 2/2). Blocking with Manifest: Plains (a face-down Plains card with no creature value) would trade a worthless 2/2 manifest for GLM47's Mishra's Factory, permanently removing a utility land from their opponent.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to block, taking 2 combat damage
annotations.betterLine: Block with Manifest: Plains to trade for Mishra's Factory, destroying an opponent's utility land at essentially no cost

annotations.description: Gem3F declined to use any abilities during combat with 0 cards in hand. They could have turned Loyal Unicorn face-up for {3}{W} to give attacking creatures vigilance and prevent combat damage to them, or used Primordial Mist to exile Enigma Sphinx and cast it for cascade value to rebuild their empty hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate any abilities during combat.
annotations.betterLine: Turn Loyal Unicorn face-up for {3}{W} to provide combat damage prevention for attacking creatures, or consider using Primordial Mist's exile ability on Enigma Sphinx if mana permits for cascade value.

annotations.description: Gem3F Optim declined to use Primordial Mist's activated ability to exile a face-down manifested creature (Loyal Unicorn or Enigma Sphinx) to play it. With 0 cards in hand and in a 1v1 against GLM47 at 15hp, converting a 2/2 manifest into a real creature (Loyal Unicorn at 3/4 for 4 mana, which is castable with available mana) would provide incremental board advantage.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate any abilities during combat
annotations.betterLine: Activate Primordial Mist to exile Manifest: Loyal Unicorn face-up, then cast Loyal Unicorn for {3}{W} using available untapped lands to get a real 3/4 creature instead of a 2/2 manifest token

annotations.description: In a 1v1 with GLM47 at 15 life vs Gem3F at 22 life, GLM47 declined to activate Mishra's Factory during combat. The opponent has no creatures to block, so attacking for 2 damage would be free value. With no instants in hand to hold up mana for, there's no reason not to attack.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate Mishra's Factory during combat, missing a free 2-damage attack.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Mishra's Factory for {1} to make it a 2/2, then attack Gem3F Optim for 2 damage, reducing them from 22 to 20.

annotations.description: Putting Eel Umbra on Paradise Druid (a mana dork) instead of Cold-Eyed Selkie in a 1v1 situation where card advantage is critical. Cold-Eyed Selkie as a 2/2 with umbra armor could draw cards on combat damage, which is much more impactful than protecting a mana dork when GLM47 already has 8 lands.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Eel Umbra targeting Paradise Druid, making it a 3/2 with umbra armor
annotations.betterLine: Cast Eel Umbra on Cold-Eyed Selkie, making it a 2/2 with umbra armor that can draw cards on combat damage - more impactful in a 1v1 endgame at 15 vs 22 life where card advantage matters more than mana production

annotations.description: Activating Mishra's Factory's pump ability ({T}: Target Assembly-Worker creature gets +1/+1) during combat with no clear valid Assembly-Worker target to pump, or if targeting itself, tapping it removes it from combat. This wastes the Factory's tap for the turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to tap Mishra's Factory to give an Assembly-Worker +1/+1 during combat
annotations.betterLine: Either activate Mishra's Factory as a 2/2 creature and attack with it, or tap it for colorless mana to use on something else, or simply hold it untapped.

annotations.description: Cold-Eyed Selkie is 8/6 without trample. Not blocking means taking 8 damage (16→8 life) AND letting the opponent draw 8 cards from Selkie's triggered ability. Blocking with even one 2/2 Manifest creature would have prevented all combat damage to the player and all card draws, since Selkie doesn't have trample.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not block, allowing Cold-Eyed Selkie to deal 8 damage and draw 8 cards
annotations.betterLine: Block with one or both Manifest creatures to prevent all combat damage and deny the massive card draw trigger

annotations.description: At 6 HP in a 1v1 against an opponent at 14 HP, Gem3F declined to cast Primordial Mist or take any other available action. With GLM47's lands all tapped, this was a safe window to develop the board. Primordial Mist would provide incremental card advantage through manifesting, and a manifest creature could serve as a blocker or enable Yuriko ninjutsu. Passing here wastes mana and tempo in a position where Gem3F is significantly behind on life.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without taking any action, leaving mana unused.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Primordial Mist to develop the board and generate card advantage through manifesting, while also potentially creating blockers or ninjutsu enablers for Yuriko.

annotations.description: GLM47 Grudge has all lands tapped and no creatures on the battlefield, meaning Gem3F could attack with both Pilgrim's Eye (1/1 flying) and the face-down Manifest (2/2) for 3 unblockable damage with zero risk. At 6 HP vs opponent's 14 HP, every point of free damage is critical.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Pilgrim's Eye and the Manifest creature for 3 free damage, bringing GLM47 from 14 to 11 HP. There is no possible downside since the opponent has no blockers and all permanents are tapped.

annotations.description: Declined to use Primordial Mist's ability to exile the face-down Loyal Subordinate and cast it this turn. While Aminatou isn't on the battlefield so the Lieutenant ability wouldn't trigger, getting a 3/1 body on board is still valuable when Gem3F is at 6 life and needs to deal 14 damage to the remaining opponent. Every creature matters in this race situation.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to use Primordial Mist's exile ability on the manifested Loyal Subordinate
annotations.betterLine: Use Primordial Mist to exile the manifested Loyal Subordinate face-up, then cast it for {2}{B} using untapped lands to get an additional 3/1 attacker/blocker on board

annotations.description: Primordial Mist's end step trigger allows Gem3F to manifest the top card of their library for free, creating a 2/2 creature. At 6 life with only lands on the battlefield and facing potential threats, declining a free 2/2 body is giving up value for no reason. Even if the manifested card isn't a creature that can be flipped, a 2/2 blocker could be the difference between surviving another turn or not. This is a pure-upside ability with no downside.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to manifest the top card of their library from Primordial Mist's trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Accept the Primordial Mist trigger and manifest the top card, getting a free 2/2 creature that could serve as a blocker or be flipped face-up later.

annotations.description: Selecting Kenrith's Transformation to return with Mantle of the Ancients attaches it to their own creature, turning it into a 3/3 Elk that loses all abilities. While it does contribute +1/+1 from Mantle's count and draws a card on ETB, it removes the creature's native abilities and sets base power/toughness to 3/3, which is counterproductive when trying to build a voltron threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected all 4 targets including Kenrith's Transformation to return with Mantle of the Ancients
annotations.betterLine: Select only Shielding Plax, Robe of Stars, and Abundant Growth - all provide pure upside (hexproof, phasing protection, card draw, mana fixing) without the downside of turning the creature into a vanilla 3/3 Elk.

annotations.description: Mishra's Factory is already tapped, so animating it into a 2/2 creature serves no purpose - it can't attack or block meaningfully this turn. This wastes 1 mana that could be spent on other plays.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Mishra's Factory to become a 2/2, despite it being tapped and unable to attack.
annotations.betterLine: Skip the Factory activation and use that mana for other plays like casting Wild Growth on a land to ramp toward Netherese Puzzle-Ward, or simply save the mana.

annotations.description: Activating Robe of Stars to phase out a creature during precombat main when the only remaining opponent (Gem3F Optim) is at 6hp with no creatures. This wastes mana and potentially removes an attacker that could be pressuring the opponent toward lethal.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Robe of Stars to phase out equipped creature
annotations.betterLine: Activate Mishra's Factory to make it a 2/2 creature, then attack Gem3F Optim to apply pressure toward the 6 damage needed for lethal

annotations.description: In a 1v1 situation (both other players eliminated), Gem3F Optim chose not to attack with any creatures despite GLM47 Grudge having no available blockers (Mishra's Factory and most lands tapped). Attacking with all four creatures would deal 9 damage (1+2+4+2), bringing GLM47 from 14 to 5 HP. Being at 6 HP themselves, this free damage would dramatically shift the game in their favor.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose not to attack with any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all creatures (Pilgrim's Eye, both Manifests, and Conundrum Sphinx) for 9 unblocked damage, putting GLM47 at 5 HP and creating near-parity in life totals.

annotations.description: Gem3F Optim declined Primordial Mist's end step trigger to manifest the top card of their library for free. At 6 life in a 1v1 against an opponent at 14 life, a free 2/2 creature serves as a blocker or attacker at no cost. This is pure upside - there's no reason to decline it.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to manifest the top card of library from Primordial Mist's end step trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Accept the manifest trigger to get a free 2/2 creature (Loyal Subordinate face-down). At 6 life, every blocker matters, and Primordial Mist can later exile it face-up to cast it properly.

annotations.description: Wild Growth on a basic Forest produces {G}{G} from one land tap. Enchanting Azorius Chancery would produce {W}{U}{G} from one land tap - 3 mana total and better color diversity, since the Chancery already produces 2 mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Enchanted a basic Forest with Wild Growth
annotations.betterLine: Enchant Azorius Chancery with Wild Growth to get 3 mana ({W}{U}{G}) from a single land tap instead of just {G}{G}

annotations.description: GLM47 declined to activate Mishra's Factory during combat when Gem3F Optim is at 6 life with no creatures to block. In this 1v1 situation with both other players eliminated, every point of damage matters. Attacking for 2 would put the opponent to 4 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate Mishra's Factory, missing 2 damage against an opponent at 6 life with no blockers.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Mishra's Factory to make it a 2/2, then attack Gem3F Optim for 2 damage, putting them to 4 life.

annotations.description: Gem3F Optim declined to block Cold-Eyed Selkie with their Manifest creature (2/2), taking 27 lethal combat damage when at 6 life. Cold-Eyed Selkie has islandwalk but Gem3F controls no Islands (their lands are Sejiri Refuge, Plains, Tranquil Cove, Command Tower, Isolated Watchtower, Orzhov Guildgate, Plains, Dimir Guildgate - none with Island subtype), so the Selkie could have been blocked. Without trample, all 27 damage would have been absorbed by the 2/2 blocker, keeping Gem3F alive.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to use the Manifest creature (Loyal Subordinate) as a blocker, taking 27 lethal combat damage.
annotations.betterLine: Block Cold-Eyed Selkie with the Manifest (Loyal Subordinate) 2/2 creature to absorb all combat damage and survive.
